citations.description: Ticket comment by RebarBotNava (timestamp 1788412934808409001): 'Block only objective defects (substantial exact duplication, unsummarized transcript dumps, structurally empty updates); keep length, near-duplication, filler, paragraph length, alternative sprawl, and imperative density advisory.' No computable signal, threshold, severity level, or exemption is stated for any individual check.

findings.criterion: For each proposed check, state its computable signal, default threshold, severity, and exemption.
findings.detail: The ticket comment's Recommendation paragraph categorizes checks into blocking vs. advisory groups but does not enumerate the four required attributes (computable signal, default threshold, severity, exemption) for each individual check. It names checks such as 'substantial exact duplication', 'unsummarized transcript dumps', 'structurally empty updates', 'length', 'near-duplication', 'filler', 'paragraph length', 'alternative sprawl', and 'imperative density' — but provides none of the per-check specifics the criterion demands.
findings.remediation: Add a structured table or list in the ticket comment that, for each proposed check, explicitly states: (1) the computable signal (e.g., exact string match ratio ≥ X%), (2) the default threshold (e.g., >30% overlap), (3) the severity (e.g., blocking/advisory/info), and (4) the exemption condition (e.g., 'exempt if content is a quoted reference').
findings.title: Per-check attributes (signal, threshold, severity, exemption) not provided

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
